core.title: Make each tracking-plan item's identity mirror its path
core.given: Telemetry is adopted, and a tracking-plan item file exists under the telemetry root. The root's default location and its configured override come from the profile; a configured root replaces the default. The file may be new, changed or unchanged.
core.when: You plan, author, rename or review a tracking-plan item at <telemetry root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>]
core.then: Make the item's declared identity mirror its path: id = telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}], logical_artifact = telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, and the file name's kind, plane and measure equal the declared fields.
prefer: Name the file for what it is, then derive id and logical_artifact from the path.

Keep the item valid against the stack's tracking-plan schema, whose location comes from the profile (layout.schemas#tracking_plan). Declare id, a SemVer version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties and required. Optionally add forbidden_properties. Give each property a type, classification and cardinality. Every `required` name must be declared in `properties`. Metric dimensions are optional, but each one present must declare cardinality.
Give every metric item a measure segment (metric.<plane>.<measure> in the file name, id ending :{measure}). Never give an event, trace or log item a measure segment.
avoid: Renaming a file or hand-editing an id so that the path and the identity drift apart
Declaring the same concrete id in two files
Putting notes, indexes or generated bundles under the telemetry root
Treating a logical artifact as an exporter event
unless: Telemetry is not adopted: there is no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration. Adoption means creating the tree or making the first acceptance decision.
core.why: The telemetry tree is a registry, not a suggestion. The path is the authority for identity, so a renamed file or a hand-edited id cannot drift apart silently.
evidence: Every tracking-plan item file under the resolved telemetry root validates against the tracking-plan schema (location from the profile: layout.schemas#tracking_plan).

For each file, the kind, plane and measure parsed from the file name match the declared fields. The id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] and the logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, both derived from the path.
No concrete id is declared by more than one file.
With no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration, the check emits no findings.
In an adopted repository, an unchanged item that is invalid is still reported. Checks cover all items, not only changed ones.
Every metric item has a measure segment in its file name and id. No event, trace or log item has one.
verification: Severity 2, strict disposition: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
Scope: the telemetry root, the versioned tracking-plan source of truth, resolved through the profile. A configured root replaces the default and does not add to it; only the resolved root is scanned.

Item path grammar: <telemetry root>/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>] with the item file suffix taken from the profile's item pattern. Metric items carry a measure segment; event, trace and log items never do.

Division of labor: local shape is the tracking-plan schema's job — required identity fields, URN grammar, SemVer core version, property declarations with classification and cardinality, and metric dimensions that declare cardinality. The schema's location is profile data (layout.schemas#tracking_plan). This rule covers the cross-artifact checks the schema cannot see: (1) the file name's kind, plane and measure match the declared fields; (2) the id equals telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}] derived from the path; (3) the logical_artifact equals telemetry:{theme}:{artifact} from the path; (4) the names in `required` are a subset of the `properties` keys; (5) no two files declare the same concrete id.
Item fields: id, version, logical_artifact, kind, plane, owner, purpose, acceptances, properties, required. Optional: forbidden_properties and, for metrics only, dimensions.

Identity model: a concrete item is a telemetry URN with kind and plane, telemetry:{kind}:{plane}:{theme}:{artifact}[:{measure}]. A logical artifact, telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, is the stable architectural identity of an observable outcome; it is not an exporter event — the concrete items under it are.
Every file of the tracking-plan item format under the root is judged as an item. There is no allow-list for non-item files of that format.
Adoption gate: with no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration anywhere, emit nothing. Installing or upgrading the convention tooling must not fail a repository that has not opted in.
After adoption, the check covers all items under the resolved root regardless of diff status; an unchanged item that is invalid is still reported.

values: telemetry adopted: a telemetry root exists, or an acceptance declares telemetry

fires: A planner adds a new tracking-plan item file under the telemetry root for a new observable outcome
A tracking-plan item file is renamed or moved, and its id or logical_artifact no longer matches its new path
An existing, unchanged tracking-plan item in an adopted repository has an id that does not match its path
A metric item has no measure segment, or an event, trace or log item has one
The repository configures a non-default telemetry root, and an item under that configured root is checked
doesNotFire: The repository has no telemetry root and no acceptance declares telemetry (it has not opted in)
Item files outside the resolved telemetry root, including files under the default root when a different root is configured
Files under the telemetry root that are not of the tracking-plan item format

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the telemetry (tracking-plan) registry lives: the default root, the config knob that overrides it, and that the override replaces the default rather than adding to it. This is a second, simultaneous plan registry alongside the one carried by roots.plan, which in this stack is bound to the source plan root.

Location of the schema document that defines the tracking-plan item format and owns its local-shape validation (required identity fields, URN grammar, version, property declarations, metric dimensions). The core's references to 'the tracking-plan schema' bind to this entry.

neutralityNotes: The telemetry data model — kinds (event/trace/metric/log), planes, measures, the item field list and the telemetry:{...} URN grammar — is treated as stack-neutral convention content, because the tracking plan is an ATDD artifact whose shape does not depend on the runtime; only its serialization suffix is profile data. All profile requirements use existing vocabulary v3 keys (no proposals): roots.telemetry and layout.locations#telemetry_item are used rather than roots.plan and layout.plan_item because a profile holds one value per key and this stack runs two simultaneous plan registries — the plan-root registry already occupies both slots — so the telemetry registry gets its own entries; layout.schemas#tracking_plan carries the tracking-plan schema document's location so other profiles can bind their own schema. What could not be made neutral: the default root path and its config knob (profile: roots.telemetry, declared in roots.config), the concrete item path pattern including the .json suffix (profile: layout.locations#telemetry_item), the tracking-plan schema document location telemetry-plan.schema.json (profile: layout.schemas#tracking_plan; only the JSON Schema validation technology itself remains bunOnly in verifier_detail[2]), the adoption finding id telemetry_adopted (bunOnly), and the worked fix example (bunOnly: verifier_detail[8]). Severity 2 and the strict disposition are kept in core verification, not the profile, per the not-profile-keys rule; the validator ref planner_telemetry_plan stays with the realization.
